study type: Validation study (of registry data using medical records as reference standard)
exposure: Pregnancy-related variables (parity, pre-gestational BMI, diabetes disorders, previous cesarean section, hypertensive disorders)
Delivery-related variables (obstetric surgical procedures, pharmacological pain-relief, gestational age at delivery)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 1264 women who gave birth in the Region of Southern Denmark during 2017.
finding: Obstetric coding in the Danish National Patient Register exhibits very high validity and completeness, making it a valuable resource for epidemiologic research.
mod_finding: Delivery-related variables, including obstetric surgical procedures such as cesarean section and induction of labor, demonstrated high positive predictive values (0.98-1.00) and sensitivities (0.87-1.00).
cross-section timing: Data was reviewed for births occurring during 2017.
birth_weight: Birthweight was one of the infant-related variables evaluated for validity, showing a PPV of 1.00.
gest_age: Gestational age at delivery was one of the delivery-related variables evaluated for validity, showing high PPVs (0.98-1.00) and sensitivities (0.87-1.00).
